productDirection.summary: Canvas Fogworks is both a general visual/pixel editor and a game-authoring environment.

items.summary: Record a Windows Sandbox pass, on DESKTOP-2SB8IKI, of the extended installer lifecycle (legacy 0.0.4 project migration, assisted GUI per-user and per-machine install/uninstall, silent per-machine install/uninstall) and a separate host hardware-GPU validation. The guest writes result.json through the staged Node writer and sets status passed only when that file already meets the guest half of check:installer-evidence, including the current installer SHA-256 and smoke logs whose stdout contains a packaged smoke pass; a rejected pass removes a previous status passed file. validate:hardware-gpu exits 0 only when --out hardware-gpu.json was re-read and already meets the host half (hostname, recordedAt, virtualGpu not-used, hardware classification recomputed from the renderer). Assisted clicks try UI Automation invoke or selection first; per-machine phases fail closed unless the guest is elevated. No extended Sandbox result.json or host hardware-gpu.json has been recorded. Exit 2 with no files remains the open manual gate rather than a pass. The September 7 per-user software-rendered synthetic-upgrade pass did not cover those phases. Virtual GPU stays disabled. Personal publisher metadata and signing remain intentionally omitted.

Continue extracting cohesive panels and workflows from App.tsx. The layers panel, document toolbar (theme, state, timeline, light, background, screen), project files, image-sequence import, workspace/runtime controls, the 3D inspector, the folders drawer, the script and token panels, the timeline transport, the node inspector sections for states, slots, variants and metadata, and the import-placement callbacks (folder images, numbered sequences, Aseprite, SVG paths and tile maps) are tested seams. App.tsx still owns the rest of the inspector, the canvas and tools, the runtime play loop, selected-node track import, and 3D model and HDR environment import.

Extend delivered schema-88 gameplay (graphs through callable functions, lifecycle and custom events, typed entity and current-level variables, named inputs, 2D/3D interaction/spawning/checkpoints and current-level progress). Player-progress v6 now keeps visited-level snapshots and game-scoped values across transitions; v1–v5 saves still load. The editor and both players now rebind those named inputs from a Controls panel and store version-1 bindings outside the document; malformed settings fall back to the defaults. A package or caller can name up to eight previous content hashes and the progress versions those saves may use. Document schema 90 stores that same list, the inspector authors it, and export stamps the authored list onto the package the runtime honors. Only that explicit list is rewritten onto the current build, and loading it does not by itself write the new slot. Forced kills of the progress writer at partial-write, flush, pre-rename, post-rename and directory-fsync leave a fresh process able to read the last committed slot. That is not a power-loss proof or a GUI renderer crash. Full prefabs remain open.

Delivered clean-profile standalone 3D acceptance, custom font packaging, unsupported-feature diagnostics, unsigned release provenance, embedded sound playback and screen-space 2D text in the packaged 3D view. Buffer, image and HDR payloads can be streamed beside the manifest and read when a level asks for them; glTF/GLB JSON and fonts stay inline, and the 32 MiB payload budget is unchanged. The acceptance smoke removes the source and font directories, then checks WebGL presentation, packaged font registration, drawn overlay text, a played embedded cue and a path-free provenance record. check:player-exe-evidence scores a clean-machine unpacked EXE record covering WebGL, Stop, the packaged font, overlay text, the embedded cue, path-free provenance, a level transition and a streamed payload. No such record is in the repo, and exit 2 with no file is the open manual gate rather than a pass. check:package-signature verifies a detached statement only when a certificate, a publisher string, a signature and a byte-identical trust-anchor certificate are all supplied. A missing certificate or a missing publisher exits 2 and is not a pass. The exporter still stamps authenticity unsigned with null publisher, signature and certificate; no release certificate or publisher identity is in the repo, and a test key is not a product signature. An optional world-partition block can name an anchor cell, load and unload radii, and streamed buffer, image or HDR payloads inside the existing 32 MiB budget. The session loads those chunks when a caller sets the focus, cancels a read the focus leaves, keeps the anchor when a neighbor fails, and refuses a larger residency budget. The packaged player validates the block and does not feed it a camera position. A package without the block is not world-partition streamed; check:world-partition exit 2 is not a pass. Signatures and publisher identity remain open without a real certificate and publisher, camera-driven world-partition paging remains open, and the complete F1 gate remains open.

Extend delivered OBB/sphere contacts and opt-in gravity/restitution with dynamic-body impulses, angular dynamics, slopes/character behavior, hierarchical collider transforms and a replaceable backend boundary.
Extend delivered embedded sound cues and bounded Web Audio playback with a total decoded-byte cache budget, streaming music, buses and dedicated reusable audio assets.

Delivered browser recovery restore, desktop crash/relaunch automation, transactional dependency-folder rollback, and measured durability checkpoints on top of bounded linked-level/image/3D relocation. Atomic replacement flushes the temporary file, flushes its directory when the platform allows it, writes a checksummed commit marker, and flushes that directory again before renaming over the destination. After that marker directory flush has returned, discarding the rename because its directory flush has not returned leaves the new bytes installable by the next replacement when the destination is still the previous version. A different newer explicit save is not replaced by that marker. A crash before the marker's directory flush returns can still drop the new name: the next replacement deletes the temporary file because it has no marker. Dependency payload bytes are fsynced, then a checksummed filesSynced record is appended to the existing journal and that append's file sync returns, before the journal name is removed. A torn tail is ignored. Once that file sync has returned, discarding the journal unlink because its directory flush has not returned still shows filesSynced, and rollback keeps the copies. A crash before that file sync returns can still show the previous in-progress record and roll the copies back. The next cross-folder Save As still deletes only files and directories an in-progress journal created. A journal that still says filesSynced keeps those copies and removes only itself. filesSynced means those file sync calls returned. Recovery does not replace Save and does not apply over a newer explicit save. Power-loss durability is still not claimed: a disk that ignores flush can still lose bytes that sync reported, a platform that refuses directory fsync can still drop a new name, and a crash before the commit marker's directory flush returns can still drop a new name. Renamed self-linked entry files and external image URLs stay refused; project relocation does not copy custom fonts.

Informational release budgets stay frozen from the September Windows Iris Xe sample and the 2026-09-28 Linux Xeon run, using CPU/GPU, 1024 raster, 500-instance, 100-mesh and disk-reload benchmarks plus a mixed soak, noisy 2048 rasters, larger textured scenes and exact history JSON accounting. Additional host samples are stored beside those budgets and do not move them. The original Linux host has no hardware WebGL; llvmpipe stays a separate software record and is not a hardware budget. A later 2026-09-28 cloud Xeon VM recorded another CPU sample, an unavailable WebGL context, and a labeled llvmpipe sample from unsafe SwiftShader; those three files do not move the frozen budgets. scripts/preview-hardware-admission.js prints the source edit for a later physical GPU sample and does not apply it. No stored sample is classified hardware, a sample file cannot attest a physical machine, and software GL stays ineligible. A 2026-10-05 check of the three host-sample files, the published September Iris Xe table, and git history found no unclassified physical-GPU sample to admit. Those September GPU p95 values are already the frozen cohort; the unmasked renderer string was not retained, so preview-hardware-admission.js --summary reports readyForOperatorAttestation 0 and frozenGpuCohort.refileable 0, and the numbers were not re-admitted. No hardware-independent CI gate is enabled. Still missing is a later physical GPU host's measured benchmark with a retained renderer string, one p95 each for Signal Garden, relay, and 100 meshes, and an operator attestation that the machine is physical. One such host would still leave the gate off. These samples do not justify a renderer rewrite.
Decide whether SVG and Canvas need WebGL-equivalent per-fragment mesh-relief normals and self-occlusion; flat-surface scene lighting is now shared.

3D many-light path: frames now keep up to 1024 authored lights and each draw is shaded by its strongest 16/8/4 reachable lights (tier chosen from MAX_FRAGMENT_UNIFORM_VECTORS), replacing the fixed 4-per-frame cap; covered by unit tests and smoke:many-lights (400 point lights, Electron Chromium on one desktop GPU). Still open: selection is per draw, not per pixel, so one large mesh under many bulbs gets only the budget (a clustered/data-texture path would fix that); point lights cast no shadows; no frame-time numbers have been measured for hundreds of lights or on weak/mobile GPUs.
Implement minmax/fit-content tracks and remaining explicit grid-placement refinements.
Restore incremental dirty-state reuse for documents containing component instances.
Defer AI, full plugins and collaboration until production-hardening work is established.
